chunks: Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was brought a man from Taghlib who had become Christian after his Islam, and they testified against him. So Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said to him: “What do these witnesses say?” He said: “They have spoken the truth, and I return to Islam.”

He said: “Indeed, if you had denied the witnesses, I would have struck your neck. But I have accepted it from you, so do not return; and if you return, I will not accept from you any return after that.”

key_terms.أَرْجِعُ: I return, meaning he declared his return to Islam.
key_terms.إِسْلَامِهِ: His state of Islam before committing apostasy.
key_terms.الشُّهُودُ: The witnesses whose testimony established the case.
key_terms.تَنَصَّرَ: He became Christian after previously being Muslim.
key_terms.رُجُوعًا: A return, here meaning repentance and re-entry into Islam.
key_terms.لَضَرَبْتُ عُنُقَكَ: I would have struck your neck, an expression indicating execution.

ai.seo_question: What did Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام rule regarding a man who returned to Islam after apostasy?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal case before Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning a man who apostasized after embracing Islam and then admitted the testimony against himself. Upon his return to Islam, his repentance was accepted once, with a warning that if he were to relapse again, no further return would be accepted from him. The narration is significant in discussions of the legal rulings concerning apostasy and judicial procedure in Shia fiqh.
